timing: CUDA graphs, preallocated plans, rotated order, warm buffers, no locked clocks. Full backward includes dY preparation, any W preparation, X quantization, both GEMMs, output cropping and bias reduction.

implementation.cta_output_tile: 8R x C in original dX[M,K] coordinates
implementation.warp_accumulator: C x R for swapAB; R x C for direct AB
implementation.loads: TMA BF16 dY and original FP8 W. Only producer loads global scales, consumers read shared scales.
implementation.compute: Native transposing byte LDSM weight quads feed QMMA A directly. Online dY quantization becomes B, preserving row/N32 scales.
implementation.epilogue: Logical transpose of accumulator base tiles, FP32->BF16, STSM.16.MT88.4, asynchronous TMA store to original dX[M,K].
implementation.default_tiles: R16/BK64, C64 if C128 cannot create at least one CTA per SM, otherwise C128; narrower aligned config for incompatible output strides.
implementation.weight_padding: No W transpose and no reduction-row padding. Widths incompatible with standard TK swizzled descriptors retain row-padding fallback.
implementation.remaining_preparation: prepare_dy still produces padded dY and transposed/padded dY for the two gradients.
implementation.api: GemmLibrary.plan_ab(...,swap_ab=True); LinearBackwardPlan defaults to swapAB unless transpose_weight=True; swap_ab=False selects the previous direct AB path. FP8Linear default backend remains Triton.

validation.oracle: Independent quantized CPU FP64 reference; all nine tile configs, actual TMA row tails, persistent buffer reuse over long K, zero/changed weights and scales, strided tensors, CUDA streams/graphs and compiled autograd. Six performance shapes match the transpose baseline bitwise for dX/dW/db.
validation.initcheck_note: Test TMA destinations are initialized with NaN to check output coverage and accommodate missing TMA-store initialization tracking. Runtime does not fill outputs.

assembly.method: Lexical last-register-definition audit plus producer/consumer position checks in emitted unrolled SASS; not a general control-flow analyzer.
